approaches.name: Serialized spine with frozen shared registries, then waves by owned directory
approaches.summary: One coder builds the greenfield spine alone (#1, #27, #2, #26, plus empty registries for statuses, error codes, config keys, router mount and Alembic chain). Later waves fan out only where each story owns its own package. Money-moving and pod-dependent stories go last, and blocked spikes are deferred.
approaches.how:
Wave 0 (serial, one coder): #1 scaffold with ALL known deps pinned up front (pyproject/uv.lock, package.json/lock) + #27 settings + #2 data layer incl. status.py, error_codes.py, money.py, config_keys.py + #26 CI.
Wave 1 (parallel, disjoint dirs): #3 pipeline/, #4 auth/, #5 integrations/fusion/, #28 services/config/, #40 locks, #29 observability, #31 web/lib/api.
Wave 2: stations #6/#34, #7, #8/#9, #10, #11, #14, #18, #30 and UI #19-#22, each in its own module; routers auto-registered from api/<pkg>/api/routers/ so main.py is never edited.
Wave 3 (money path, serial-ish): #13, #15, #16, #17, #38, #39, #35; one Alembic revision per story, merger re-points down_revision and gates on `alembic heads` == 1.
Defer/stub: #12, #33, #39 tenant check, #43 (needs off-repo source data), #24 runs, #25/#44 plan-only.
evidence: Greenfield repo: every parallel coder would otherwise create pyproject.toml, uv.lock, package.json, main.py and alembic/env.py at once; lockfiles do not merge textually.
Alembic linear history breaks with parallel revisions (multiple heads); Oracle DDL auto-commits, so a half-failed migration leaves partial schema on DEV ATP and cannot roll back.

CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 7 (one status enum, one StageRunner, one chat component): parallel coders inventing their own copies is the predicted defect; prior lessons §5 says reporting drifted from the matcher last time.
Stories #3, #6-#18 all import status, error codes, config and the repository base; building them before #2/#28 forces guessed interfaces.
#12 blocked on pod name, #33 on mail platform, #39 on tenant confirmation, #5/#17/#38 require live non-prod confirmation per CLAUDE.md 'never guess an endpoint'.
risks: Wave 0 is a long serial critical path; a defect in the spine propagates to every later story.
Registry files (status.py, error_codes.py, config_keys.py) still get appended by several stories; needs append-only sections or one-file-per-domain to avoid conflicts.
Deferring pod-dependent stories leaves FusionClient calls stubbed; stubs risk being mistaken for confirmed contracts.

approaches.name: Rails-first: money and data safety guards land before any feature that can move cash
approaches.summary: Treat the cash-moving path as the highest risk and build its guard rails as foundation code: Decimal fidelity end to end, an apply kill-switch defaulting off, a production-pod refusal, reservation and idempotency ledger, fail-closed SOAP parsing, safe artifact parsing and PII-free logging. Feature stories may only call Fusion writes through these rails.
approaches.how:
In #2/#27: oracledb fetch_decimals=True and Numeric(asdecimal=True); money serialized as strings in Pydantic/OpenAPI so web never sees floats; LLM schema amounts as strings parsed to Decimal.
In #5: FUSION_WRITE_ENABLED=false default, environment allowlist that refuses prod pods (shared by #23, #32, #35 dry-run), fail-closed SOAP via defusedxml, typed error mapping.
In #2/#13/#15: APPLICATION_LEDGER table (receipt_id, trx_id, amount, idempotency key, unique constraint) written before and reconciled after each apply; SKIP LOCKED reservation with lease expiry.
In #4: JWT alg pinned to JWKS RS256, iss/aud/exp/nbf checked, group-claim name verified live; #29 redaction filter + test before any station logs; #34 zip-bomb, path-traversal and nested-depth limits.
Readers get no tools; artifact text is untrusted (prompt injection) and only structured output is accepted; chat actions re-authorized in the API.
evidence: python-oracledb returns Oracle NUMBER as float unless defaults.fetch_decimals is set; float money silently violates the CLAUDE.md Decimal rule.
JSON numbers become JS doubles in web/; amounts must cross the API as strings to stay exact.
Prior lessons §4 defects: no cap, no reservation, no ambiguity check, no idempotency, re-sent message re-applied, partial apply never resumed.
Prior lessons §3/CLAUDE.md: SOAP faults arrive inside HTTP 200; fail-closed parsing is mandatory. XML from Fusion and .msg/.eml/zip from email are untrusted input (XXE, zip bombs).
Remittance artifacts come from external senders, so text inside them can attempt prompt injection against Opus/Haiku; CLAUDE.md requires zero data retention and no PII in logs.
risks: Guard code front-loads effort before visible features; reviewers may trim it as over-engineering.
A kill-switch default of off means end-to-end tests on the non-prod pod need an explicit per-environment enable, which must itself be audited config.
Ledger uniqueness rules must match Fusion's real application semantics (partial applies, unapply in #38) or they block legitimate retries.

approaches.name: Maximum parallelism: one coder per story, vertical slices from day one
approaches.summary: Dispatch all unblocked stories at once, each coder scaffolding what it needs and the merger resolving conflicts. Fastest wall clock on paper, highest conflict and drift risk.
approaches.how:
Spawn ~35 coders in parallel worktrees off sprint/<slug>.
Each creates its own models, migration, router and UI page.
Merger serializes merges and resolves lockfile, Alembic-head and enum conflicts by hand.
Shared abstractions extracted afterwards in a refactor story.
evidence: Repo is empty: there is no existing BaseRepository, StageRunner, status enum or settings class to converge on, so slices would each invent one.
CLAUDE.md states a second copy of shared behaviour is a defect, so the refactor is guaranteed rework.
Lockfiles (uv.lock, package-lock.json), alembic/versions heads and FastAPI main.py would conflict on nearly every merge.
risks: Duplicate status/error enums diverge (the exact prior failure) and money handling becomes inconsistent across stations.
Multiple Alembic heads and partial Oracle DDL on DEV ATP that cannot be rolled back.
Security rules (token validation, PII logging, prod-pod guard) implemented unevenly or not at all per slice.
